title: Integer-orbit free pairs and the explicit adjunction
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal V$. Let $\mathcal A$ be a category with $\mathcal V$-small morphism sets and $\mathbf Z$-indexed coproducts, and let $T:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ be an autoequivalence with a chosen quasi-inverse. Write $P_n=T^n$ for integer powers, $P_0=\mathrm{id}$, and $c_{n,M}:T(P_nM)\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{n+1}M$ for the identity or quasi-inverse counit identifications. Let $\mathcal A^T$ and $U$ denote the fixed-pair category and forgetting [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]. There is a functor $A:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A^T$ with carrier $UA(M)=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}P_nM$, carrier map $UA(f)=\bigoplus_nP_n(f)$, and structure isomorphism $\sigma_M:T(UA(M))\xrightarrow{\sim}UA(M)$ characterized, for the coprojections $\iota_{n,M}$, by $\sigma_M\circ T(\iota_{n,M})=\iota_{n+1,M}\circ c_{n,M}$. The functor $A$ is left adjoint to $U$. The adjunction bijection is restriction to the zeroth summand:
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A^T}(A(M),(X,\theta))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M,X),\qquad a\longmapsto Ua\circ\iota_{0,M}.$$
For each $a_0:M\to X$ there is a unique family $a_n:P_nM\to X$, indexed by all integers and having prescribed zeroth member $a_0$, with $a_{n+1}\circ c_{n,M}=\theta\circ T(a_n)$. The inverse bijection has carrier $\coprod_na_n$. These bijections are natural in both variables. If $\mathcal A$ is preadditive with biproducts and $T$ is additive, $A$ is additive for the inherited addition on morphisms of fixed pairs.

proof.text: Reuse the existing Free.functor, Free.objMap and Free.str constructions in the source library. The carrier and carrier-map identities are definitional. Free.map_ι_comp_str gives the displayed shift equation. These are the fixed-pair and coproduct constructions [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category, def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

For uniqueness of the structure isomorphism, apply Iso.ext and Free.map_hom_ext. The latter is coproduct extensionality after applying the coproduct-preserving equivalence [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits]. The two composites with each F(ι_n) coincide by the assumed equation and Free.map_ι_comp_str.

Prove local family extensionality: if a and b obey the recurrence, then a_m=b_m if and only if a_(m+1)=b_(m+1). Forward, cancel the epimorphism c_m and use the two recurrence equations. Backward, cancel the monomorphism θ and use faithfulness of F [lem-sf-quasi-inverse-hom-bijection]. Integer induction starting at zero proves equality at every index, including the negative-to-zero crossing. Take Free.hom K a0 as the family; Free.hom_zero and Free.map_hom_comp_str give its properties, and local family extensionality gives uniqueness.

Take the existing Free.adjunction F, constructed by Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. The mkOfHomEquiv_homEquiv equation exposes its hom equivalence: restriction to the zeroth summand, with inverse Free.desc. The carrier of Free.desc is Sigma.desc (Free.hom K a0). Local family extensionality identifies Free.hom K a0 with every family satisfying the prescribed zeroth member and recurrence, yielding the required inverse formula. Apply homEquiv_naturality_left and homEquiv_naturality_right for the two naturality clauses.

Under the additive hypotheses [def-weil-preadditive-category, def-weil-pbc-additive-functor], use the inherited preadditive structure on fixed pairs. To show Free.functor.map(f+g)=Free.functor.map(f)+Free.functor.map(g), apply Free.hom_ext, so only restrictions to the zeroth summand remain. On this summand objMap is the original morphism, and Sigma.ι_map together with bilinearity gives the equality. This is exactly Functor.Additive; separate proofs of additivity for the quasi-inverse and all nonzero iterates are unnecessary.

lean.statement: theorem fixedPairFreeIntegerAdjunction {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (F : C ⥤ C) [F.IsEquivalence] [HasColimitsOfShape (Discrete ℤ) C] : (∀ M : C, ((Free.functor F).obj M).carrier = ∐ (Free.obj F M)) ∧ (∀ (M N : C) (f : M ⟶ N), ((Free.functor F).map f).hom.f = Limits.Sigma.map (Free.objMap F f)) ∧ (∀ (M : C) (n : ℤ), F.map (Sigma.ι (Free.obj F M) n) ≫ ((Free.functor F).obj M).str.hom = (Free.objSucc F M n).hom ≫ Sigma.ι (Free.obj F M) (n + 1)) ∧ (∀ (M : C) (σ : F.obj (∐ (Free.obj F M)) ≅ ∐ (Free.obj F M)), (∀ n : ℤ, F.map (Sigma.ι (Free.obj F M) n) ≫ σ.hom = (Free.objSucc F M n).hom ≫ Sigma.ι (Free.obj F M) (n + 1)) → σ = ((Free.functor F).obj M).str) ∧ (∀ (M : C) (K : IsoAlgebra F) (a0 : M ⟶ K.carrier), ∃! a : (n : ℤ) → (Free.obj F M n ⟶ K.carrier), a 0 = a0 ∧ ∀ n : ℤ, (Free.objSucc F M n).hom ≫ a (n + 1) = F.map (a n) ≫ K.str.hom) ∧ (∃ adj : Free.functor F ⊣ forget F, (∀ (M : C) (K : IsoAlgebra F) (a : (Free.functor F).obj M ⟶ K), adj.homEquiv M K a = Sigma.ι (Free.obj F M) 0 ≫ a.hom.f) ∧ (∀ (M : C) (K : IsoAlgebra F) (a0 : M ⟶ K.carrier) (a : (n : ℤ) → (Free.obj F M n ⟶ K.carrier)), a 0 = a0 → (∀ n : ℤ, (Free.objSucc F M n).hom ≫ a (n + 1) = F.map (a n) ≫ K.str.hom) → ((adj.homEquiv M K).symm a0).hom.f = Sigma.desc a) ∧ (∀ (M N : C) (f : M ⟶ N) (K : IsoAlgebra F) (a : (Free.functor F).obj N ⟶ K), adj.homEquiv M K ((Free.functor F).map f ≫ a) = f ≫ adj.homEquiv N K a) ∧ (∀ (M : C) (K L : IsoAlgebra F) (a : (Free.functor F).obj M ⟶ K) (b : K ⟶ L), adj.homEquiv M L (a ≫ b) = adj.homEquiv M K a ≫ (forget F).map b)) ∧ (∀ [Preadditive C] [HasFiniteBiproducts C] [F.Additive], (Free.functor F).Additive)
